From b7c510d049049409e8945b932f4b0b357fa17415 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2024 18:42:38 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] arm64/ptrace: Don't flush ZA/ZT storage when writing ZA via
 ptrace

When writing ZA we currently unconditionally flush the buffer used to store
it as part of ensuring that it is allocated. Since this buffer is shared
with ZT0 this means that a write to ZA when PSTATE.ZA is already set will
corrupt the value of ZT0 on a SME2 system. Fix this by only flushing the
backing storage if PSTATE.ZA was not previously set.

This will mean that short or failed writes may leave stale data in the
buffer, this seems as correct as our current behaviour and unlikely to be
something that userspace will rely on.

Fixes: f90b529bcbe5 ("arm64/sme: Implement ZT0 ptrace support")
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240115-arm64-fix-ptrace-za-zt-v1-1-48617517028a@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c b/arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c
index 20d7ef82de90..b3f64144b5cd 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c
+++ b/arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c
@@ -1107,12 +1107,13 @@ static int za_set(struct task_struct *target,
 		}
 	}
 
-	/* Allocate/reinit ZA storage */
-	sme_alloc(target, true);
-	if (!target->thread.sme_state) {
-		ret = -ENOMEM;
-		goto out;
-	}
+	/*
+	 * Only flush the storage if PSTATE.ZA was not already set,
+	 * otherwise preserve any existing data.
+	 */
+	sme_alloc(target, !thread_za_enabled(&target->thread));
+	if (!target->thread.sme_state)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	/* If there is no data then disable ZA */
 	if (!count) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c`**
- The code that unconditionally flushes the buffer used to store ZA (the zero-accumulating register) has been modified. 
- The `sme_alloc` function is now called with a condition that checks if PSTATE.ZA was already set. If it was set, the existing data in the buffer is preserved instead of flushing it.
- The error handling for memory allocation remains the same, returning `-ENOMEM` if the allocation fails.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a bug where writing to ZA could corrupt the value of ZT0 when PSTATE.ZA was already set. By changing the flushing behavior to only occur when PSTATE.ZA is not set, the patch prevents this corruption.
- The change reflects a shift in handling the state of the ZA storage, allowing for potential stale data to remain in the buffer after short or failed writes, which is deemed acceptable in this context. This adjustment is intended to maintain data integrity for the ZT0 register while still allowing for the correct operation of the ZA register.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
sme_alloc(target, true);
```
```c

```
```c
target->thread.svcr &= ~SVCR_ZA_MASK;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `sme_alloc` function is called with `true`, which unconditionally flushes the buffer used to store the ZA register. This leads to the corruption of the ZT0 register if PSTATE.ZA is already set, as the buffer is shared between ZA and ZT0. The subsequent check for `target->thread.sme_state` does not prevent the flush from occurring, resulting in unintended data loss.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
sme_alloc(target, !thread_za_enabled(&target->thread));
```
```c
if (!target->thread.sme_state)
```
Reason:
The fix modifies the call to `sme_alloc` to conditionally flush the storage only if PSTATE.ZA was not already set, by using `!thread_za_enabled(&target->thread)`. This change ensures that if ZA is already active, the existing data in the buffer is preserved, preventing the corruption of the ZT0 register when writing to ZA.
